title: This 3,000-Year-Old Toe Could Walk
viewerLearnsAtEnd: A three-part ancient Egyptian wooden-and-leather toe was probably a functional prosthesis worn in life, not merely a burial decoration.

claims: Cairo toe dated 950–710 BC; three-part wood and leather.
Replica gait tests used two volunteers missing the right big toe and replica Egyptian sandals.
Both volunteers could walk; one achieved nearly 78% of normal toe flexion with the wooden design.
Conclusion remains qualified as one of history's earliest working prostheses.
sources: University of Manchester, 14 Feb 2011: Mummies’ false toes helped ancient Egyptians walk.
University of Manchester, 2 Oct 2012: Egyptian toes likely to be the world’s oldest prosthetics.
University of Basel LHTT: Wooden toe prosthesis from TT95.
